subject: Clarify auto-renew notice flow & termination-for-convenience path
messages:
From: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T08:03:00Z
Subject: Order form questions: auto-renew and exit options

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for sending over the latest order form. Procurement and Legal at Acme are reviewing but had two quick questions on the term/exit mechanics before we proceed:

1) Auto-renew: The order form currently renews automatically for successive 12-month terms unless notice is provided 90 days before the end of term. Can Redwood accept a 60-day notice window instead? Our internal process requires shorter notice for certain pilot buys.

2) Termination for convenience: We need to know whether termination for convenience is permitted on the Order Form at all, and what, if any, commercial obligations (e.g., pro-rated payment, transition assistance) would apply if Acme opts to terminate during a term.

We attached a purchase order reference for the PO team. If helpful, can your team propose language we can take to our legal team?

Thanks —
Maya Singh
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
(purchase_order_4321.pdf attached)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Order form questions: auto-renew and exit options

Hi Maya —

Appreciate the quick read-through and the PO. Looping in Ben (Account Exec) and Marissa (Legal) to propose the clean language and commercial options. High-level from my side: we're open to discussing a 60-day notice for this order but would like to preserve the standard 90-day window on multi-year/enterprise contracts. For termination for convenience, we typically allow it on Order Forms with a limited set of transition obligations — Marissa will confirm.

Can you confirm whether this is for a pilot/short-term engagement (<=12 months) or a committed 12+ month purchase? That will help drive our suggested tradeoffs.

I'll follow up by EOD with proposed wording we can both present to legal.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T14:02:00Z
Subject: RE: Order form questions: auto-renew and exit options (internal)

Rishi/Ben —

Thanks for the tag. Quick read and proposed approach below (internal comments + redline attached — MSA_Redline_Termination_v2.docx).

Summary / risk posture:
- Auto-renew: 60-day notice materially increases churn risk for long commitments. For a pilot or one-year order we can accept 60 days with a shorter notice cap included in the Order Form. For any committed multi-year term, we should keep 90 days.
- Term for convenience: We can permit it on Order Forms only (not the underlying MSA) with a simple commercial remedy: (i) 30 days' written notice; (ii) payment of all fees through the effective date; (iii) a pro-rated termination fee equal to 30% of remaining committed fees (negotiable). We should also require a standardized transition assistance clause (30 days limited support).

Suggested clause (Order Form friendly):
"Termination for Convenience. Customer may terminate the Order Form for convenience upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice. Upon termination: (a) Customer shall pay any fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination; (b) if the Order Form includes a minimum committed term, Customer will pay a termination fee equal to thirty percent (30%) of remaining committed fees; and (c) Redwood will provide up to thirty (30) days of transition assistance at Redwood's standard professional services rates."

Alternate concession to offer (commercial): 60-day auto-renew notice in exchange for either (A) firm 12-month minimum commitment OR (B) a one-time transition credit equal to 10% of the first-year fees. The credit can be included as a line-item on the order form.

Flag for Sales: if we agree to 60 days without a commitment, ask for a TCV or right to convert to reserved (Dedicated) if usage > X tokens — operationally we want to avoid churn on high-usage customers.

Attachments: redline doc includes MSA paragraph numbers and a clean + tracked version for the Order Form.

Happy to jump on a quick call with Acme legal if Ben/Rishi want.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-23T09:20:00Z
Subject: RE: Order form questions: auto-renew and exit options (internal)

All — quick commercial take:

- Goal: keep the commit where it matters but close the deal quickly. Acme is a strategic pilot for us; I'd prefer we offer the 60-day notice for this Order Form.
- Concessions to offer to Acme: 60-day renewal notice + 30% pro-rated termination fee OR 60-day notice + no termination fee but a one-time onboarding/transition credit (10% of year-1).
- Negotiation playbook: open with the 60-day + 30% fee language (Marissa's suggested language). If legal pushes back, swap to 60-day + 10% credit (commercial equivalent).
- Operational asks: if accepted, require a short SLA addendum that caps free transition assistance at 30 days and documents the escalation contacts. Ask Product/Onboarding to pre-prepare a 30-day offboarding checklist.

I can present the proposed language on a call tomorrow at 11am PT with Maya and their legal lead. Rishi — want me to take the call and close?

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-24T16:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Order form questions: auto-renew and exit options

Hi Maya / Acme team —

Thanks for the questions and the PO. After internal review, here's a proposal intended to keep the pilot flexible while protecting both teams operationally:

1) Auto-renew: For this Order Form only (pilot/12-month term), Redwood will accept a 60-day written notice to opt out of renewal. For any subsequent renewal beyond year one, Redwood requests a 90-day notice for enterprise commitments.

2) Termination for Convenience: We can include a termination-for-convenience clause on the Order Form with the following terms:
   - 30 days' written notice;
   - Customer pays fees for services rendered through the effective termination date; and
   - If the Order Form included a minimum committed term, a termination fee equal to 30% of remaining committed fees.

Commercial concession (optional): In lieu of a 30% termination fee, Redwood will offer a one-time transition credit equal to 10% of year-1 fees (to be applied as a credit on the invoice) if Acme prefers.

Operational note: Redwood will provide up to 30 days of transition assistance at standard rates (we can include a short SLA addendum).

Attached: OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf with the proposed language tracked. Please confirm whether you prefer the 30% fee or the 10% credit and we will circulate a redline. Ben can take a call to finalize — he is available tomorrow at 11am PT if you'd like to discuss.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf)
